items.summary: Recommendation: maintain financial containment and reject both proposed CRO initiatives this cycle. Do not authorize new spend, forecasts, commitments, monetization expansion, or revenue claims. Revenue evidence covers 2026-09-21 only: 6,219 clicks, 28 ordered items, 6 shipped items, and $4.92 aggregate commission. The aggregate row is not site-attributable; reported site-attributed commission is $0, which does not prove zero site performance. Contribution margin, ROI, payback, cost-to-learn, infrastructure spend, and budget exposure are not calculable: revenue and cost periods do not align; AI-cost records conflict ($881.36 across 4,832 calls for 2026-09-01 through 2026-09-27 versus retained $973.35 across 5,439 calls); infrastructure, domain, labor, marketing, approved-budget, experiment-cost, and defined learning-outcome records are absent or incomplete. Treat impressions, rankings, clicks, sessions, conversions, ordered items, shipped items, performance scores, and AI calls as operating metrics, not financial returns. Continue only the existing reconciliation work using recorded telemetry. Minimum measurement: period-aligned attributable revenue by tracking ID and site/content, one reconciled AI-cost ledger, infrastructure/domain/labor/marketing/approved-budget/experiment-cost records, and a defined learning outcome with cost and success threshold. Budget status remains unbounded because monthly spend and budget limits are blank.

The two CRO control-plane proposals are retained only as deferred backlog for operational usefulness, not as financial investments. Their stated metrics concern linkage coverage, duplicate follow-ups, reconciliation effort, and unsupported green-light decisions; no revenue, margin, ROI, payback, or causal lift should be inferred. Reconsider only after existing failure containment and measurement reconciliation produce a clean prototype gate and a defined cost-to-learn threshold.
